placements.why: Nothing in the supplied (empty) strata or graph structure covers instrument calibration/verification as an organizational category. This envelope's content — a spectrograph calibrated and verified against reference plates — names a durable operational category (calibration records, verification against benchmarks) rather than a one-off fact, and future envelopes about other instruments' calibration would plausibly nest here. Minted standalone per the strata-mint rule: no parent required.
placements.title: Instrument calibration as its own organizational category

placements.title: Calibration status is established by verification against a named external benchmark
placements.frame: what benchmark or reference standard is an instrument's calibration being verified against, and does it hold across the full operating range?
placements.why: Both src-1 and src-2 assert the same directional theme — the Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration at 88.4 MHz is established and validated by checking against the June reference plates, holding across the full observing band. This is a subject future calibration envelopes will keep feeding (new instruments, new reference sets, re-verifications), not a one-time measurement — it passes the narrative grain test. No existing leaf was supplied to reuse, so minted fresh under the newly-minted Calibration strata.
